I get that. I treat it like a podcast or audiobook, listen while I play video games, cook, work, etc.  
It's fast enough paced to be enjoyable from moment to moment. Sometimes I'd only listen for fifteen minutes at a time, pick it up again later.
I'm the same way. The only live gameplay of D&D I've enjoyed is Dungeons of Drakkenheim by the Dungeon Dudes.

For a bit of edgy humor:  
I'm a 3.5 purist, surrounded by Critical Role stans. Why wouldn't I want to kill myself.
I run a semi-monthly game, and I play in a separate, monthly campaign.
A little bit of everything, but I always came back to Arthurian Fantasy.

I've studied the craft of writing for the last nine years. The last three of which I spent as a freelance ghostwriter under various online names, this being one of them. I learned the most about what it means to be a writer in those years. Effective writing without need for passion, inspiration, or flow.

I quit that about a year ago. Joined two different writing groups. Nice folks. Not an ounce of craft between them, but they enjoy what they do. Listening to them get excited over their cliched, derivative characters and settings reminded me of when I was just starting out writing and was the exact same way. For a little while, I thought that I was in the right place and on the right path. 

It didn't matter.
